docs.text: Driver BASIS 2 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the Alicat BASIS 2 gas mass flow meters (B series) and controllers (BC series). It reads flow, temperature and totals, sets setpoints and valve holds, and speaks both the ASCII protocol and Modbus RTU behind one API, on any MCU. docs.text: API guide ¶ The API by task. Every call returns Result<T> (a value and an Error ) or a bare Error ; every call is noexcept . The code blocks are compiled by the host build. For every class and member see the API reference . Datasheet sections this page relies on From Alicat Scientific, Inc. DOC-MANUAL-BASIS2 Rev 4: Data frame: Data Frame Format, p. 10 Query specific data: Query Specific Data, p. 11 Setpoint, setpoint source and ramp: Setpoint; Setpoint Source; Maximum Setpoint Ramp Rate, p. 11 Communication watchdog: Communication Watchdog, p. 12 Hold valve, gains, reference temperature, averaging: Hold Valve Position; Loop Control Gains; Reference Temperature; Readings Averaging, p. 13 Measurement triggering, averages and ranges: Configure Measurement Triggering; Start a Measurement; Measurement Averages and Ranges, p. 13 Tare and autotare: Taring the Instrument; Using Ground to Tare; Autotare, p. 14 Active gas: Active Gas, p. 15 Totalizer and batch: Totalizer Reset; Totalizer Batch; Totalizer Configuration, p. 15 Full scale flow, serial number, firmware: Full Scale Flow; Unit ID; Version Number, p. 16 Unit ID: Unit ID, p. 16 Modbus address, baud rate, command protocol: Modbus Address; Serial Baud Rate; Command Protocol, p. 17 Engineering units: Reference, Engineering Units, p. 31 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Objects ¶ A Bus<Port> owns one serial line and runs one transaction at a time. A Basis2<Port> is one instrument on a bus, described by a Config . Neither does any I/O when constructed. alicat_basis2 :: Bus < MyPort > bus ( port ); alicat_basis2 :: Basis2 < MyPort > meter ( bus ); // unit ID 'A', 38400 baud, ASCII Several Basis2 objects with different unit IDs (or Modbus addresses) can share one bus. Call bus.SetDeviceCount(n) when more than one instrument is connected, so that a unit ID change is refused. Start up ¶ EnsureInitialized() brings the port up (nothing is sent). Begin() learns the instrument and is the first call that sends. Both can be repeated; after a failure they start from the beginning, and once Begin() has succeeded every other call may be used. alicat_basis2 :: Error BringUp ( Meter & meter ) { // EnsureInitialized() starts the port; Begin() learns the instrument (identity, full scale, // firmware). Both can be called again: after a failure they start from the beginning. auto r = meter . EnsureInitialized (); if ( r ) { r = meter . Begin (); } if ( ! r ) { std :: printf ( "BASIS 2 start-up: %s \n " , alicat_basis2 :: ToString ( r . error )); } return r . error ; } Begin() reads the serial number, firmware, full scale and its unit, the gas, the setpoint source and the ramp (read commands only), and checks the first data frame. After it, GetIdentity() returns an Identity : the kind (meter or controller), firmware, full scale, flow unit and label, gas and source. IsReady() is false while the state is unknown, and IsStateUnknown() tells that case apart. Read ¶ Call Returns ReadFrame() The whole frame: flow, temperature, total, for a controller setpoint and valve drive, gas and flags ReadFlow() , ReadTemperature() , ReadTotal() One Decimal ReadValveDrive() , ReadSetpointValue() , ReadBatchRemaining() One Decimal (controllers) ReadStatus() StatusFlags : mass_flow_over , temperature_over , totalizer_over , valve_hold , valve_thermal ReadData(items) A frame with only the items you ask for (a DataItem mask) A Decimal is an integer mantissa and a count of decimals, so nothing is lost to floating point; ToDouble() and ToMilli() convert. Values are in the instrument's own flow unit, which GetIdentity().unit_label prints. A flow beyond Config::flow_margin_permille of the full scale, or a temperature outside the plausibility limits, is OutOfRange and no value is returned. Reads are retried up to Config::read_retries times after a failed transaction; nothing that changes the instrument is ever retried. Set a setpoint ¶ alicat_basis2 :: Error RampTo ( Meter & meter , double flow ) { // The unsaved source never wears the non-volatile memory; the saved one is rate limited. if ( auto r = meter . SetSetpointSource ( alicat_basis2 :: SetpointSource :: UnsavedDigital ); ! r ) { return r . error ; } return meter . SetSetpoint ( flow ). error ; // read back and compared when no ramp is active } The setpoint is checked against 0 to 2.5 % over full scale before anything is sent, and read back unless a ramp is active. A meter returns Unsupported . While the source is saved a change sooner than three minutes after the last is RateLimited . Read Safety notes before you move a valve. Other tasks ¶ Task Calls Hold or release the valve HoldValve() , OpenValve() , CloseValve() , ResumeControl() (ASCII only) Ramp SetRamp(rate, unit) , DisableRamp() , ReadRamp() Tare Tare(duration_ms) , TareDefault() , SetAutotare() Gas SetGas() , ReadGas() , ReadGasList() ( GasName() names the nine gases) Totalizer and batch ResetTotal() , SetTotalizerLimit() , SetBatch() , DisableBatch() Reference temperature, averaging SetReferenceTemperature() , SetAveraging() Measurement window SetMeasurementTrigger() , StartMeasurement() , ReadAverages() , ReadRanges() Identify ReadSerialNumber() , ReadFirmware() , ReadFullScale() Scan ScanUnitIds() (ASCII), ScanModbusAddresses() (Modbus) Raw access, for diagnostics ReadRegisterRaw() (Modbus), ReadRawLine() (ASCII), GetLastReply() (no I/O) The raw reads send one request and never retry; a reply is still accepted only after its CRC, address and length (or unit ID) check. GetLastReply() returns the last reply any call accepted, without touching the bus. ScanUnitIds() and ScanModbusAddresses() block for the whole scan: 26 polls, each up to a reply wait, or one read per address. Run them from a task that may wait, and not from a loop with a deadline. Guarded commands ¶ alicat_basis2 :: Error MoveToUnit ( Meter & meter ) { // Commands that can strand the instrument need a token that names the consequence. return meter . ChangeUnitId ( 'B' , alicat_basis2 :: ConfirmUnitIdChange {}). error ; } The six guarded commands are listed with their tokens in Safety notes . Recover ¶ void Resynchronise ( Meter & meter ) { // After an unexplained failure: find the instrument again (scans unit IDs or Modbus addresses). if ( auto r = meter . Recover (); ! r ) { std :: printf ( "BASIS 2 recover: %s \n " , alicat_basis2 :: ToString ( r . error )); } } Recover() finds the instrument again after a guarded command that was not confirmed or an unexplained failure: it polls the configured ID or address and, when the bus declares one instrument, scans the unit IDs over ASCII or the Modbus addresses over Modbus. It then relearns the identity and compares the serial number, firmware and kind with the earlier ones: another instrument is VerifyMismatch . The state stays unknown ( IsStateUnknown() ) until all of that succeeds. Handle errors ¶ Error values 0 to 9 are the base set shared by every driver of the organisation; values from 16 are this driver's. const char * Describe ( alicat_basis2 :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case alicat_basis2 :: Error :: Timeout : return "no reply: check wiring, unit ID, baud rate and RS-485 direction control" ; case alicat_basis2 :: Error :: DeviceIdMismatch : return "another unit answered: check the unit ID or Modbus address" ; case alicat_basis2 :: Error :: Crc : return "line noise: check cabling and termination" ; default : return alicat_basis2 :: ToString ( e ); } } Error Meaning What to do Bus Write() returned false Check your port Timeout No complete reply in time Wiring, A and B, baud rate, unit ID, direction pin: Troubleshooting DeviceIdMismatch Another unit answered Two instruments with one ID Crc Modbus CRC-16 mismatch Line noise, termination BadReply , Overflow The line does not match the grammar, or has no end A wrong protocol, a wrong baud rate, noise Rejected The instrument answered ? or a Modbus exception The command is not valid in this state or on this model OutOfRange A decoded value is impossible Check the unit and the decimals VerifyMismatch The read-back differs from what was set A ramp, a clamp, or an analog source FirmwareTooOld The call needs a newer firmware Update or FirmwareGate::Ignore RateLimited A saved setpoint came too soon Use the unsaved source StateUnknown , GuardNotConfirmed A guarded command is not settled, or the token is wrong Recover() Busy The bus was not free, or the line never went quiet: the transaction that met it was not sent. A writing call returns it only when its write was not sent Wait, retry; find the peer that talks Unsupported Not on this protocol, this kind, or this port Check the table above Not blocking ¶ Bus can also be driven without blocking: Submit() a request, call Poll() from your loop and Take() the result. Basis2 itself calls Execute() , which waits. Take every result before the next Basis2 call: Execute() drops a result nobody took (its transaction is over) and waits at most as long as the transaction on the bus can still take. See Porting . Next: Configuration .

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is built: a serial bus that owns the line, an instrument object on top of it, and a port you write. What happens in each layer when you read a flow. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Alicat Scientific, Inc. DOC-MANUAL-BASIS2 Rev 4: Default serial settings and the link layer: Alicat ASCII Serial Communication, Establishing Communication, p. 10 Modbus RTU framing, address and baud: Modbus-RTU; Communicating Via Modbus-RTU; Changing the Baud Rate, p. 18 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/alicat_basis2.hpp public calls ; inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp UartInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . Layers ¶ Layer Files Owns Instrument inc/alicat_basis2.hpp , src/alicat_basis2.ipp Basis2<Port> : one instrument; the typed API, learning, verification, guarded commands, scans Bus inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp , src/alicat_basis2_bus.ipp Bus<Port> : one serial line, one transaction at a time, timing, quarantine, stray bytes Codecs inc/alicat_basis2_ascii.hpp , inc/alicat_basis2_modbus.hpp , inc/alicat_basis2_request.hpp Request factories, reply grammars, CRC-16, the independent wire validators Types and registers inc/alicat_basis2_types.hpp , inc/alicat_basis2_registers.hpp Error , Result , Config , Decimal , Frame , the Modbus register table Port contract inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp The CRTP base and the UartPort concept Platform port Your class The UART, the clock, optionally a delay, a baud switch and logging Kconfig layer inc/alicat_basis2_kconfig.hpp Optional: a Config from ESP-IDF menuconfig Bus knows the line, not the instrument; Basis2 knows the instrument, not the timing. Several Basis2 objects share one Bus when instruments share a line, and the bus lets one transaction run at a time. One call through the layers ¶ sequenceDiagram participant App as Your code participant B2 as Basis2 participant Bus as Bus participant Port as Your port App->>B2: ReadFlow() B2->>B2: ascii::Make(Poll) builds and checks the bytes B2->>Bus: Execute(request, timing) Note over Bus: wait t3.5 of silence Bus->>Port: FlushInput(), Write("A\r") loop until a CR or the deadline Bus->>Port: Read(buffer) end Port-->>Bus: "A +012.30 +024.8 ... Air\r" Bus-->>B2: Reply Note over B2: strict grammar, unit ID, range B2-->>App: Result of Decimal The transaction machine ¶ A transaction is submitted, advanced by Poll() and taken. Execute() does the three steps and waits with DelayMs() when the port has it, or spins on NowMs() . The states are Idle , Gap , AwaitReply and Settling . Gap. The line must have been silent for 3.5 character times ( 35 / baud seconds at ten bits per character, at least 1 ms) since the last byte in either direction. The instrument acts on a command only after its own 3.5 character idle time following the carriage return (manual p. 10). Send. FlushInput() , then Write() . A false from Write() is Error::Bus and nothing is pending. Await. Each Poll() reads what has arrived and appends it to a 256-byte line buffer until a carriage return or the deadline: 3.5 character times plus the line time of the longest reply plus processing_ms , or slow_command_ms for the commands that may write non-volatile memory. Settle. After a timeout, an overflow, a bad line or a wrong-ID reply the bus holds for at least one reply-wait and then until the line has been quiet for 3.5 character times plus 2 ms, with a hard deadline of two reply-waits. No command is sent until then, so a late reply of the failed command cannot be taken for the answer of the next one. A command with a known busy period (tare, factory restore, a timed valve hold) holds the bus for that period. Stray bytes. docs.text: A transaction is submitted, advanced by Poll() and taken. Execute() does the three steps and waits with DelayMs() when the port has it, or spins on NowMs() . The states are Idle , Gap , AwaitReply and Settling . Gap. The line must have been silent for 3.5 character times ( 35 / baud seconds at ten bits per character, at least 1 ms) since the last byte in either direction. The instrument acts on a command only after its own 3.5 character idle time following the carriage return (manual p. 10). Send. FlushInput() , then Write() . docs.text: Contract ¶ What the BASIS 2 driver promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. A change to anything here is a breaking change, listed under Breaking in the changelog . Datasheet sections this page relies on From Alicat Scientific, Inc. DOC-MANUAL-BASIS2 Rev 4: Default serial settings and the link layer: Alicat ASCII Serial Communication, Establishing Communication, p. 10 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Promises ¶ The constructors of Bus and Basis2 are noexcept , store their arguments, do no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() brings the port up and checks the stored configuration ( InvalidArgument , nothing sent). Begin() is the first call that sends: it learns the instrument with read commands only. On any failure the object stays not ready and the next call starts again from the beginning. Every call that sends returns Error::NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() and Begin() have succeeded where the call needs them. No call starts the instrument as a side effect. Nothing is ever sent outside the documented grammar. A Request can be made only by the factories, and every request is checked a second time by an independent validator before Write() (invariant I1). No command is sent while a transaction waits, or inside the quarantine that follows a failed one, or less than 3.5 character times after the last byte on the line (I3, I4). The six commands that can strand an instrument are sent only for a call with its confirmation token (I5). A setpoint is never negative or above 102.5 % of the full scale, a valve hold never leaves 0 to 100 percent, and a saved setpoint is never changed faster than Config::saved_setpoint_min_interval_ms (I6). A failed call returns a zero-valued result: no value from a failed or partial reply is exposed (I8). A reply is used only when its first token is the unit ID addressed; a Modbus reply only when address, function and CRC match. Writes are never repeated. Reads are repeated at most Config::read_retries times. Every wait is bounded by a deadline computed from the baud rate and Config ; Poll() always reaches a result or a terminal state within its deadlines: one line wait for a quiet line (else Busy , nothing sent, and a quarantine that needs only the quiet line), one reply wait for the reply, then the quarantine (I9). Execute() bounds both of its waits in time as well. The 32-bit millisecond clock may wrap and the line may stay quiet for weeks: every wait is a start time and a duration, compared as an unsigned elapsed time, so no wait depends on where the clock is (I11). A wait that is not polled for 2^32 ms (49.7 days) may be read as just begun and last its length once more; for the same reason a saved setpoint made exactly a multiple of 2^32 ms after the last one may be refused as RateLimited for up to saved_setpoint_min_interval_ms (the safe direction). StateUnknown is left only by a successful Recover() (I12), which needs a validated reply from the same instrument (serial number, firmware and kind unchanged). Only a switch-off ( SetSetpoint(0) , CloseValve() ) is still sent while it holds. A missing optional hook is not an error: no DelayMs() spins on NowMs() , no SetBaud() makes ChangeBaud() return Unsupported , no Log() logs nothing. A hook declared with the wrong signature is a compile error. The fuzz targets check I1, I3 and I5 to I16 after every call (I11 through the clock offsets and the long quiet periods of their sessions); I2 and I4 are proven by directed unit tests, and I9 and I11 by both ( Testing and CI ). Depends on ¶ Dependency Version Why A C++20 compiler GCC 10, Clang 13 or later Concepts constrain the port CMake 3.16 or later Generates alicat_basis2_version.h Your port A serial line at 38400 baud 8N1 or what you configure, a millisecond clock, and for RS-485 the direction control inside Write() Nothing else: no RTOS, no SDK, no other repository of the organisation. Threading ¶ The driver is not thread-safe and takes no lock. Use each Bus and every Basis2 on it from one task at a time, or guard every call with one mutex; the layer that owns the driver owns that lock. Nothing may run in an ISR. Separate buses share no state. Errors ¶ alicat_basis2::Error inside alicat_basis2::Result<T> . Values 0 to 9 are the shared base set; values from 16 are specific to this driver, and each is returned by some call (a test checks it). Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 EnsureInitialized() or Begin() has not succeeded InvalidArgument 2 An argument or a Config field is out of range; nothing was sent Bus 3 A port hook returned false Timeout 4 No complete reply within the computed time DeviceIdMismatch 5 The reply carried another unit ID or address Crc 6 Modbus CRC-16 mismatch Busy 7 The bus was not free or the line never went quiet: the transaction that met it was not sent; a writing call returns it only when its write was not sent ( Safety ) DeviceFault 8 Reserved: the instrument reports faults as flags, which are data, not errors Unsupported 9 Not available on this protocol, this kind, or this port BadReply 16 The line does not match the command's reply grammar Rejected 17 The instrument answered ? or with a Modbus exception OutOfRange 18 A decoded value is outside what the instrument can report Overflow 19 The reply exceeded the line buffer without a terminator VerifyMismatch 20 The read-back after a setter differs FirmwareTooOld 21 The call needs a newer firmware StateUnknown 22 A guarded command is not settled RateLimited 23 A saved setpoint came too soon GuardNotConfirmed 24 A guarded call carried the wrong token The API guide says what to do about each. Memory ¶ No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no std::string , no printf and no static mutable state. A Bus holds a 256-byte line buffer and a request; a Basis2 holds a Config , an Identity and the shadow state. Platform ¶ Platform-free: the same code runs on any target with a C++20 compiler, including the host tests. The ESP-IDF port in examples/esp32 is an example, not part of the driver. Deviations from the standard ¶ The port's Read() is partial. It returns the number of bytes read ( std::size_t ), not an exact-length bool , because the reply length of an ASCII line is not known in advance. Documented in Porting . The line buffer is 256 bytes, not 128 , because the gas list ( GS * ) reply can be that long. The scans block. ScanUnitIds() and ScanModbusAddresses() run to the end of the scan inside one call; every other call is bounded by one reply wait. DeviceFault is never returned. It stays in the base set, so the numeric values match the other drivers.

Every wait is bounded by a deadline computed from the baud rate and Config ; Poll() always reaches a result or a terminal state within its deadlines: one line wait for a quiet line (else Busy , nothing sent, and a quarantine that needs only the quiet line), one reply wait for the reply, then the quarantine (I9). Execute() bounds both of its waits in time as well. The 32-bit millisecond clock may wrap and the line may stay quiet for weeks: every wait is a start time and a duration, compared as an unsigned elapsed time, so no wait depends on where the clock is (I11). A wait that is not polled for 2^32 ms (49.7 days) may be read as just begun and last its length once more; for the same reason a saved setpoint made exactly a multiple of 2^32 ms after the last one may be refused as RateLimited for up to saved_setpoint_min_interval_ms (the safe direction). StateUnknown is left only by a successful Recover() (I12), which needs a validated reply from the same instrument (serial number, firmware and kind unchanged). Only a switch-off ( SetSetpoint(0) , CloseValve() ) is still sent while it holds. A missing optional hook is not an error: no DelayMs() spins on NowMs() , no SetBaud() makes ChangeBaud() return Unsupported , no Log() logs nothing. A hook declared with the wrong signature is a compile error. The fuzz targets check I1, I3 and I5 to I16 after every call (I11 through the clock offsets and the long quiet periods of their sessions); I2 and I4 are proven by directed unit tests, and I9 and I11 by both ( Testing and CI ).

docs.text: The driver is not thread-safe and takes no lock. Use each Bus and every Basis2 on it from one task at a time, or guard every call with one mutex; the layer that owns the driver owns that lock. Nothing may run in an ISR. Separate buses share no state.

docs.text: No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no std::string , no printf and no static mutable state. A Bus holds a 256-byte line buffer and a request; a Basis2 holds a Config , an Identity and the shadow state.

docs.text: The port's Read() is partial. It returns the number of bytes read ( std::size_t ), not an exact-length bool , because the reply length of an ASCII line is not known in advance. Documented in Porting . The line buffer is 256 bytes, not 128 , because the gas list ( GS * ) reply can be that long. The scans block. ScanUnitIds() and ScanModbusAddresses() run to the end of the scan inside one call; every other call is bounded by one reply wait. DeviceFault is never returned. It stays in the base set, so the numeric values match the other drivers.

docs.text: Hardware ¶ The connector, wiring for RS-232 and RS-485, power, LED, analog signals and size classes of the BASIS 2 meters and controllers, as the driver uses them. The instrument is a module with one six-pin connector, not a chip in a package, so the figures draw the connector as one row of pins. Datasheet sections this page relies on Models, ranges and options: Alicat Scientific, Inc. DOC-MANUAL-BASIS2 Rev 4, Introduction, p. 3 Mounting, LED and power-up behaviour: Alicat Scientific, Inc. DOC-MANUAL-BASIS2 Rev 4, Getting Started, Mounting, p. 5 Power and signal connections, pin 4 only: Alicat Scientific, Inc. DOC-MANUAL-BASIS2 Rev 4, Power and Signal Connections, p. 6 Connector pins and serial levels: Alicat Scientific, Inc. DOC-MANUAL-BASIS2 Rev 4, Power and Signal Connections (pin table), p. 7 Tare and autotare: Alicat Scientific, Inc. DOC-MANUAL-BASIS2 Rev 4, Taring the Instrument; Using Ground to Tare; Autotare, p. 14 Analog signals: Alicat Scientific, Inc. DOC-MANUAL-BASIS2 Rev 4, Analog Signals, p. 28 Supply current, accuracy and update rate: Alicat Scientific, Inc. DOC-SPECS-BASIS Rev 19, Technical Data, p. 1 Size classes and dimensions: Alicat Scientific, Inc. DOC-SPECS-BASIS Rev 19, Dimensions, p. 3 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Power on pin 4 only Only connect power to pin 4, and do not switch the supply on until all the other pins are connected. Power on any other pin can permanently damage the instrument (manual pp. 6 and 28). Do not connect the instrument to a loop-powered system: it will destroy parts of the circuitry. Use an isolator and a separate supply. Facts that are not verified Nothing here has been checked on an instrument. A fact that no document states is marked unverified : the JST GH pitch, whether an unused signal pin may float, the transceiver, the terminations and the decoupling of the two circuits, and the maximum supply. The connector ¶ BASIS 2 (B and BC series) pinout, JST GH 6-pin connector Figure description and sources The BASIS 2 (B and BC series) seen from the top, in its JST GH 6-pin connector package. Pin 1 is marked by the dot; the numbers run counter-clockwise from it. Each pad is coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Next to it is the pin's name and, in mono, the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it; a pin without a hook is not used by the driver. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp . JST GH 6-pin connector, 6 pins (Power and Signal Connections, pin table, p. 7 ). Pin Name Type (domain) Function Driver hook If unused Datasheet 1 A-SET 1 analog (SIGNAL) Analog setpoint input (controllers); on a meter, ground this pin for at least 25 ms to tare - Leave open Using Ground to Tare (Meters), p. 15 2 A-OUT 2 analog (SIGNAL) Analog flow output, 0 to 5 V or 4 to 20 mA by model - Leave open Analog Signals, p. 28 3 GND ground Ground, common to power, analog and serial - - Power and Signal Connections, pin table, p. 7 4 PWR power (PWR) Power in, 12 to 24 V. Power on any other pin can permanently damage the instrument - - Power and Signal Connections, p. 6 5 RX/B bus (SIGNAL) RS-232 receive (the instrument receives, unverified: the manual does not say whose side Rx names) or RS-485 B (+), by model Write() - Power and Signal Connections, pin table, p. 7 6 TX/A bus (SIGNAL) RS-232 transmit (the instrument transmits, unverified: the manual does not say whose side Tx names) or RS-485 A (-), by model Read() - Power and Signal Connections, pin table, p. 7 Source of this table and of the chip figures: docs/hardware.yml . Pin 1 does two jobs by model: on a controller it is the analog setpoint input, on a meter grounding it for at least 25 ms tares the instrument, and the tare completes when the ground is removed (manual p. 15). The serial pins carry RS-232 or RS-485 levels, decided by the model , not by software; the manual describes no TTL option, so a microcontroller UART needs a level shifter (RS-232) or a transceiver (RS-485). The driver is level-agnostic: the port owns the physical layer. Size classes ¶ BASIS 2 (B and BC series) package, JST GH 6-pin connector Figure description and sources The BASIS 2 (B and BC series) package seen from the top and, when the height is known, from the side, drawn to scale: 68.6 x 22.2 x 39.4 mm. The arrows carry the datasheet's dimensions, the dot marks pin 1 and the pads are numbered counter-clockwise from it, coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Pads sit centred on each side, evenly spaced; the datasheet's land pattern is the reference for a board. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp . Datasheet Package JST GH 6-pin connector Power and Signal Connections, pin table, p. 7 Pins 6 Power and Signal Connections, pin table, p. 7 Body size 68.6 x 22.2 x 39.4 mm Dimensions, p. 3 Variants a , b , c , d (below) Dimensions, p. 3 Supply PWR 12.0 V to 24.0 V Power and Signal Connections, p. 6 Also sold as: Variant Package Pins Size Ordering Note Datasheet a Size class a: 100 SCCM to 2 SLPM 6 68.6 x 22.2 x 39.4 mm, about 116 g ⅛ in NPT female or SAE 4 - Dimensions, p. 3 b Size class b: 5 to 20 SLPM 6 84.0 x 25.4 x 45.7 mm, about 171 g ⅜ in NPT female or SAE 6 - Dimensions, p. 3 c Size class c: 50 to 100 SLPM meter 6 95.3 x 35.0 x 48.4 mm, about 270 g ⅜ in NPT female or SAE 6 - Dimensions, p. 3 d Size class d: 50 to 100 SLPM controller 6 114.8 x 35.0 x 52.3 mm, about 350 g ⅜ in NPT female or SAE 6 options by model, not by size: analog 0-5 V or 4-20 mA; serial RS-232, RS-485 or Modbus RTU Dimensions, p. 3 From docs/hardware.yml ; pins, circuits and the block diagram: Hardware . The sheets disagree in a few cells. Revision 19 of the specification sheet (August 2026) is used here; revision 16 (March 2024) differs in dimension B of the smallest class (0.44 in against 0.53 in), in the height of the 5 to 20 SLPM class (1.83 in against 1.80 in) and in several cells of the 50 to 100 SLPM rows. Revision 19 titles itself "through 20 slpm" but lists ten ranges; whether the 50 and 100 SLPM models are still BASIS 2 is open. The process connection is ⅛ in NPT female or SAE 4 up to 2 SLPM and ⅜ in NPT female or SAE 6 from 5 SLPM. Mount the body horizontally with the flow arrow parallel to the ground, on two M3 x 0.5 holes 6 mm deep. Inside ¶ Inside the BASIS 2 (B and BC series) Figure description and sources The BASIS 2 (B and BC series)'s function blocks inside its outline. Arrows between blocks carry signals or data in the direction they point (both ways where they have two heads). The package pins stand on the left and right edges with their numbers, each wired to the block it reaches. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp . Wiring ¶ RS-485 multidrop ¶ BASIS 2 (B and BC series): RS-485 multidrop line Figure description and sources A schematic. The MCU is on the left, each of its pins level with the chip pin it connects to; above each wire is the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it. Supply pins point up to their supply and decoupling, ground pins down. Pins on the right carry the loads and the pins tied to a supply or ground; a cross marks a pin left open. A dot is a junction; wires that cross without a dot are not connected. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp . Up to 26 instruments share one line, each with its own unit ID A to Z (or Modbus address). RS-485 is half duplex on one pair: the transceiver's A line goes to pin 6 and B to pin 5. The manual describes neither the transceiver nor a termination; a 120 ohm resistor at each end of a long line is general practice. The port owns the direction control ( Porting ). RS-232 ¶ BASIS 2 (B and BC series): RS-232 point to point Figure description and sources A schematic. The MCU is on the left, each of its pins level with the chip pin it connects to; above each wire is the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it. Supply pins point up to their supply and decoupling, ground pins down. Pins on the right carry the loads and the pins tied to a supply or ground; a cross marks a pin left open. A dot is a junction; wires that cross without a dot are not connected. Drawn from: docs/hardware.yml ; inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp . One instrument per port. The MCU's TX goes through the level shifter to pin 5, where the instrument receives, and pin 6 goes through it to the MCU's RX. Unverified: the manual's pin table lists "Rx" and "Tx" without saying whose side they name; check the wiring against an instrument before first power. Pin 3 is the common ground of power, analog and serial. Serial settings ¶ Setting Value Format 38400 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit; 4800 to 115200 selectable Unit ID One letter A to Z , default A , unique on the line; duplicates corrupt data Idle before a command 3.5 characters after the carriage return; the instrument does not act earlier Digital update rate Up to 176 Hz, depending on baud rate and system Modbus Address 1 to 247 (register 45), the same line settings, functions 3, 6 and 16 Timing derived from these is on the Protocols page. Power ¶ Model Supply Current Controller 12 to 24 V on pin 4 210 mA Meter 12 to 24 V on pin 4 12 mA Either, with a 4 to 20 mA analog output plus 40 mA Allow one minute for warm-up, five for best accuracy. The manual states no absolute maximum supply, no reverse polarity protection and no ESD rating. Analog signals ¶ The analog output is 0 to 5 V or 4 to 20 mA, by model, not by software ; zero flow is about 0.010 V or 4 mA and full scale 5.0 V or 20 mA. A controller's analog setpoint input is 0 to 5 V or 4 to 20 mA for 0 to 100 percent of full scale and is used only while the setpoint source is Analog ( LSS a ). The driver reads and writes none of them. Status LED ¶ LED Meaning Solid green Power, no errors Flashing green Serial activity Fast red blink Mass flow, temperature or totalizer over range ( MOV , TOV , OVR ) Slow red blink Valve override: a hold, or thermal management ( HLD , VTM ) Operating limits ¶ Quantity Value Ambient and gas temperature 0 to 50 C Pressure Meters 0 to 145 PSIG; controllers by valve (0 to 145, LV05 0 to 100, LV08 0 to 60); maximum common mode 145 PSIG Valve Normally closed (controllers); thermal management pulses it when a setpoint gives no flow Ingress, humidity IP40, 95 % non-condensing; a 50 micron in-line filter is suggested Gases Air, Ar, CO2, N2, O2, N2O, H2, He, CH4 Reference documents ¶ Document Revision Get it Datasheet manual: Operating Manual for Mass Flow Instruments, BASIS 2 Meters and Controllers (Alicat Scientific, Inc. MANUAL+SPECS_BASIS2) Rev 16, 2024-03-01 PDF · vendor page Datasheet manual: Alicat Modbus Manual (generic, written for the classic registers) (Alicat Scientific, Inc. DOC-MANUAL-MODBUS) Rev 7, 2024-11-01 PDF · vendor page Datasheet application note: Alicat Serial Communications Primer (classic line, firmware 4v to 10v) (Alicat Scientific, Inc. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( alicat_basis2_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-alicat-basis2.git external/driver-alicat-basis2 git submodule update --init external/driver-alicat-basis2 Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-alicat-basis2 ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE alicat_basis2::alicat_basis2 ) alicat_basis2::alicat_basis2 is an alias of the alicat_basis2 INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect ALICAT_BASIS2_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver ALICAT_BASIS2_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-alicat-basis2 -B build-alicat_basis2 cmake --install build-alicat_basis2 --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( alicat_basis2 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE alicat_basis2::alicat_basis2 ) The target is alicat_basis2::alicat_basis2 in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated alicat_basis2_version.h go to include/alicat_basis2/inc/ , the template implementation to include/alicat_basis2/src/alicat_basis2.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-alicat-basis2) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-alicat-basis2 (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-alicat-basis2.git components/alicat_basis2 alicat_basis2 (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml alicat_basis2 (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : alicat_basis2 : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-alicat-basis2.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES alicat_basis2 (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then. How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/alicat_basis2_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, sources, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target, alias, install rules and the package export, or the ESP-IDF component Tool configuration _config/ Doxyfile, the docs site, Kconfig, clang-format, clang-tidy and the linters Version ¶ The version is set once in the settings file and written into alicat_basis2_version.h in the build tree at configure time. The Doxyfile ( _config/Doxyfile ) carries a copy; a host test fails when it differs. Read it at run time: const char * v = alicat_basis2 :: GetDriverVersion (); // "0.1.0" Next ¶ Quickstart runs the driver on your PC, then on your MCU; Porting writes the port for your MCU.

docs.text: Mechanization policy ¶ Where each defect class of the catalogue is caught, and how a class moves to a cheaper catch. The goal: a defect is found by the cheapest check that can find it, and reviewers spend their time on judgement, not on what a script can do. Decision rule ¶ Catch a class at the first level that can decide it without judgement, in order of cost: Lint ( tools/preflight.sh , runs in seconds, on every builder's machine). Use it when the defect is a pattern in text or syntax: a forbidden include, a MISRA rule CodeQL reports, a missing else , a parameter name, a symbol named in docs that does not exist, a missing gitlink. Test, model or mutation (host tests, the chip model's fault knobs, fuzz properties, compile-fail cases, mutants of a fix). Use it when the defect is behaviour: what the driver sends or returns when the chip or the bus misbehaves. A test is the right level when the model can be made to misbehave in exactly that way. Independent review question (a reviewer who did not write the code). Use it only for what needs judgement: whether the datasheet was read correctly, whether a state machine is complete, whether the model is independent of the driver, whether a doc claim is true. Every catalogue entry names its level under DETECTION. A class with no lint or test is a review class and costs reviewer time every round; it is a candidate for promotion. Promotion ¶ A defect that reached a reviewer or the CI of a second driver is promoted one level up: review to test, test to lint where a pattern exists. The reviewer who finds the second occurrence writes the promotion item in the round's report; the template maintainer (the agent or person that owns the template branch) implements it before the next driver's first push, or records why it cannot be mechanised in the catalogue entry. A defect that reached a third driver after its promotion means the check is wrong: fix the check first, then look at the driver. Demotion never happens by silence: a check is removed only with a catalogue note saying what replaced it. What a lint may and may not do ¶ It reports file:line , the catalogue id, and the fix. It exits non-zero on a finding, in the preflight and the gate. It has no false-positive tolerance : before merging, it runs over every finished driver and the template; any finding on a driver that CI shows clean is a false positive, and the lint is not merged until it has none (narrow the pattern; do not add an ignore list per driver). It may be conservative the other way (miss cases): then the catalogue says partial and names the review question that covers the rest. It never edits files, never skips silently (a missing tool is reported as a skipped step in the final line, and the gate treats a skipped MISRA or ESP32 step as a failure), and has a selftest with one bad and one good case. It does not replace the CI scan: CI is the final word for MISRA. Recording a new finding ¶ Append the finding to its catalogue entry (driver, review round or CI report file, finding id) and update the count and the index table; add a new entry only when no class fits. Write the check at the level the rules above give: the lint, or the test pattern (model knob, mutant, fuzz property), or the reviewer's question in the skill. Run it over the finished drivers (lint) or add the regression test that fails without the fix (test). Add a CHANGELOG.md entry under [Unreleased] and the template change is released as a new template commit; drivers take it with scaffold.py --check-drift --fix (the skills and tools are managed files), which updates the template pin in .kokeb/template.yml . Mention the catalogue id in the commit subject. The pre-push gate ¶ A driver is cleared for its first push only by kokeb-tools/gate.sh <chip> (the orchestrator's script, one run per driver through the shared Docker lock). It writes a log and a verdict, and PASS needs all of: container preflight ( tools/preflight.sh --container ) with 0 failure(s) and 0 gate failure(s) , including the MISRA scan and the ESP32 builds; a skipped MISRA or ESP32 step is a FAIL; handbook_check reports 0 errors (this includes the library-subset include scan); tools/check_standalone.py passes; template drift: scaffold.py --check-drift reports nothing; no .pdf file is tracked; the examples/esp32/scripts gitlink (mode 160000) is present; the tree is staged as it will be committed. No silent skips: every step prints a line, and a missing tool fails the gate. Roles ¶ Builders write code, models, tests and docs and run host tests and the quick preflight. They do not run the container gate, push, or create repositories. The gate runner is one serialized worker that runs gate.sh for one driver at a time and reports the verdict and the log; it does not edit the driver. Reviewers are read-only and independent. They are given the code, the model, the datasheet, the catalogue and the previous round's report, and never the builder's conclusions (the build report is read only in the claims-vs-code step). They run the review-round protocol. Fixers change the driver, fix at the cause, add the test that fails without the fix, and answer each finding id. The template maintainer applies promotions and keeps the catalogue current. docs.text: Where each defect class of the catalogue is caught, and how a class moves to a cheaper catch. The goal: a defect is found by the cheapest check that can find it, and reviewers spend their time on judgement, not on what a script can do.
docs.title: Mechanization policy

docs.text: Catch a class at the first level that can decide it without judgement, in order of cost: Lint ( tools/preflight.sh , runs in seconds, on every builder's machine). Use it when the defect is a pattern in text or syntax: a forbidden include, a MISRA rule CodeQL reports, a missing else , a parameter name, a symbol named in docs that does not exist, a missing gitlink. Test, model or mutation (host tests, the chip model's fault knobs, fuzz properties, compile-fail cases, mutants of a fix). Use it when the defect is behaviour: what the driver sends or returns when the chip or the bus misbehaves. A test is the right level when the model can be made to misbehave in exactly that way. Independent review question (a reviewer who did not write the code). Use it only for what needs judgement: whether the datasheet was read correctly, whether a state machine is complete, whether the model is independent of the driver, whether a doc claim is true. Every catalogue entry names its level under DETECTION. A class with no lint or test is a review class and costs reviewer time every round; it is a candidate for promotion.

docs.text: A defect that reached a reviewer or the CI of a second driver is promoted one level up: review to test, test to lint where a pattern exists. The reviewer who finds the second occurrence writes the promotion item in the round's report; the template maintainer (the agent or person that owns the template branch) implements it before the next driver's first push, or records why it cannot be mechanised in the catalogue entry. A defect that reached a third driver after its promotion means the check is wrong: fix the check first, then look at the driver. Demotion never happens by silence: a check is removed only with a catalogue note saying what replaced it.
docs.title: Promotion

docs.text: It reports file:line , the catalogue id, and the fix. It exits non-zero on a finding, in the preflight and the gate. It has no false-positive tolerance : before merging, it runs over every finished driver and the template; any finding on a driver that CI shows clean is a false positive, and the lint is not merged until it has none (narrow the pattern; do not add an ignore list per driver). It may be conservative the other way (miss cases): then the catalogue says partial and names the review question that covers the rest. It never edits files, never skips silently (a missing tool is reported as a skipped step in the final line, and the gate treats a skipped MISRA or ESP32 step as a failure), and has a selftest with one bad and one good case. It does not replace the CI scan: CI is the final word for MISRA.

docs.text: Append the finding to its catalogue entry (driver, review round or CI report file, finding id) and update the count and the index table; add a new entry only when no class fits. Write the check at the level the rules above give: the lint, or the test pattern (model knob, mutant, fuzz property), or the reviewer's question in the skill. Run it over the finished drivers (lint) or add the regression test that fails without the fix (test). Add a CHANGELOG.md entry under [Unreleased] and the template change is released as a new template commit; drivers take it with scaffold.py --check-drift --fix (the skills and tools are managed files), which updates the template pin in .kokeb/template.yml . docs.text: A driver is cleared for its first push only by kokeb-tools/gate.sh <chip> (the orchestrator's script, one run per driver through the shared Docker lock). It writes a log and a verdict, and PASS needs all of: container preflight ( tools/preflight.sh --container ) with 0 failure(s) and 0 gate failure(s) , including the MISRA scan and the ESP32 builds; a skipped MISRA or ESP32 step is a FAIL; handbook_check reports 0 errors (this includes the library-subset include scan); tools/check_standalone.py passes; template drift: scaffold.py --check-drift reports nothing; no .pdf file is tracked; the examples/esp32/scripts gitlink (mode 160000) is present; the tree is staged as it will be committed. docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the port. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Alicat Scientific, Inc. DOC-MANUAL-BASIS2 Rev 4: Connector pins and serial levels: Power and Signal Connections (pin table), p. 7 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver never calls your SDK. It calls hooks on a class you derive from alicat_basis2::UartInterface<Self> (in inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp ). The base uses CRTP and declares no hook itself; the driver template is constrained by the alicat_basis2::UartPort concept, so calls are resolved at compile time (no virtual functions, nothing to allocate) and a missing or misdeclared hook is a compile error at the point of use. What you implement ¶ Method Required Contract bool EnsureInitialized() noexcept yes Bring the UART up on the first call; return true at once afterwards bool Write(const uint8_t* data, std::size_t len) noexcept yes Send all len bytes; return after the last byte has left the pin std::size_t Read(uint8_t* data, std::size_t capacity, uint32_t timeout_ms) noexcept yes Return the bytes that have arrived, up to capacity ; do not wait for more bool FlushInput() noexcept yes Drop every received byte not read yet uint32_t NowMs() noexcept yes A monotonic millisecond clock; it may wrap void DelayMs(uint32_t ms) noexcept no Sleep at least ms ; without it blocking calls poll NowMs() bool SetBaud(uint32_t baud) noexcept no Change the line speed; needed only by ChangeBaud() void Log(LogLevel, const char* message) noexcept no Print one line; message is plain text, never a format string The port ¶ my_port.hpp class MyPort : public alicat_basis2 :: UartInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the UART up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_uart_init (); } return ready_ ; } bool Write ( const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_uart_write ( data , len ); } // Whatever has arrived, up to `capacity` bytes. The driver polls, so do not wait for a full // frame. std :: size_t Read ( uint8_t * data , std :: size_t capacity , uint32_t timeout_ms ) noexcept { static_cast < void > ( timeout_ms ); return platform_uart_read ( data , capacity ); } // Drop stale bytes before each request. bool FlushInput () noexcept { return platform_uart_flush_input (); } // The driver times every wait against this clock. uint32_t NowMs () noexcept { return platform_millis (); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Rules the port must follow: Raw bytes only. The driver builds the lines and frames and checks them; the port does not parse, frame or retry. Read() is partial and does not wait. It returns what has arrived. The driver polls, keeps its own time and applies its own deadlines. (This differs from the template's exact-length Read() : the length of an ASCII line is not known in advance.) timeout_ms is advisory. Write() returns after the last byte has left the pin. The driver times the silent interval from the end of your Write() , and an RS-485 direction pin must not be released early. FlushInput() really flushes : the driver calls it before each request so a stale byte cannot shift a reply. 8N1, no flow control , at the speed in Config::baud . Bus requirements ¶ The driver states what the instrument needs from the line as constexpr values in inc/alicat_basis2_uart_interface.hpp (handbook KB-CPP-123). Check your port settings against them with static_assert , as both example ports do: Constant Value Meaning kPortDefaultBaud 38400 The factory baud rate, 8N1 (manual p. 10) kMinBaudRate , kMaxBaudRate 4800, 115200 The rates the instrument offers (p. 17) kSilentBitTimes 35 The idle time before the instrument acts, 3.5 characters of ten bits (p. 10) kTurnaroundUs 50000 Added to every reply wait (an assumption) kSupplyMinMv , kSupplyMaxMv 12000, 24000 The supply on pin 4 only (p. 6) RS-485 ¶ An RS-485 instrument is half duplex on one pair, and the driver knows nothing about the direction pin: the port owns it. Two rules follow. Switch the transceiver to transmit before the first byte and back to receive after the last byte has left the shift register , not after it has been copied to a FIFO. On ESP-IDF that is the RS-485 half-duplex mode with uart_wait_tx_done() ; on STM32 the hardware driver-enable or the transmission-complete interrupt; on Linux TIOCSRS485 . A transceiver whose receiver stays enabled while it sends hears its own bytes. Set Config::echo to EchoMode::Skip and the driver drops a first reply line that equals the command it just sent. A termination of 120 ohm at both ends of a long line and a common ground are general practice; the manual does not describe them ( Hardware ). Baud switching ¶ ChangeBaud() sends the baud command and then calls your SetBaud() right after the send, because the instrument's reply arrives at the new speed (manual p. 17). Without a SetBaud() hook the call returns Unsupported . On failure the driver sets the old speed back once and the state is StateUnknown ; call Recover() after you have checked the port's speed. Control pins ¶ None. The instrument has no reset or enable pin on its connector, and the driver sets no pin. The port is the whole platform interface. Optional hooks ¶ every hook class FullPort : public alicat_basis2 :: UartInterface < FullPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return platform_uart_init (); } bool Write ( const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_uart_write ( data , len ); } std :: size_t Read ( uint8_t * data , std :: size_t capacity , uint32_t timeout_ms ) noexcept { static_cast < void > ( timeout_ms ); return platform_uart_read ( data , capacity ); } bool FlushInput () noexcept { return platform_uart_flush_input (); } uint32_t NowMs () noexcept { return platform_millis (); } // Optional: lets blocking calls yield instead of spinning. Without it they poll the clock. void DelayMs ( uint32_t ms ) noexcept { platform_sleep_ms ( ms ); } // Optional: needed by ChangeBaud(), which changes the line speed after the instrument has // switched. bool SetBaud ( uint32_t baud ) noexcept { return platform_uart_set_baud ( baud ); } // Optional: one line per lifecycle event or failure. The driver never formats; the port does. void Log ( alicat_basis2 :: LogLevel level , const char * message ) noexcept { if ( level > alicat_basis2 :: LogLevel :: Warning ) { return ; } platform_log ( message ); // plain text: never use it as a format string } }; A hook that is declared with the wrong signature fails a static_assert that names it: a DelayMs that takes a uint16_t , or a SetBaud that returns void , is a compile error rather than a silently ignored hook. Non-blocking use ¶ Basis2 calls Bus::Execute() , which blocks until the transaction is over (with DelayMs() when the port has it). If your loop left a transaction on the bus, Execute() waits for it within its deadlines (reply wait, quarantine, hold-off) and drops its result when nobody took it, so a switch-off is never held back by it. Bus can also be driven from your own loop: // The non-blocking form: submit once, call Poll() from your loop, take the reply when it is no // longer Pending. Basis2 uses Bus::Execute(), which does exactly this and waits with DelayMs() or // the clock. alicat_basis2 :: Error StartPoll ( alicat_basis2 :: Bus < FullPort >& bus ) { const auto request = alicat_basis2 :: ascii :: Make ( alicat_basis2 :: Command :: Poll , 'A' , alicat_basis2 :: ascii :: Args {}, false ); if ( ! request ) { return request . error ; } return bus . Submit ( request . value , alicat_basis2 :: Timing {}); // Busy while another transaction is not over } bool Step ( alicat_basis2 :: Bus < FullPort >& bus , alicat_basis2 :: Result < alicat_basis2 :: Reply >& out ) { const alicat_basis2 :: PollState state = bus . Poll (); if (( state == alicat_basis2 :: PollState :: Done ) || ( state == alicat_basis2 :: PollState :: Failed )) { out = bus . Take (); return true ; } return false ; } Reference implementations ¶ Every port lives with its example, in examples/<platform>/ ; the driver has none. Platforms lists them and how to add one. examples/host/host_alicat_basis2_port.hpp : any PC, against a simulated instrument. Start from it for a host build or a test bench. examples/esp32/main/esp32_alicat_basis2_port.hpp : ESP-IDF, with every hook and an RS-485 mode. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: the ports on this page are compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over them. Call EnsureInitialized() and Begin() : Ok proves that writes and reads work and that the unit ID and baud rate are right. Call ReadFrame() once a second and open the valve of a flow source: the flow rises. Unplug the instrument: Timeout , and no stray output on the line afterwards. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each driver object one owner task, or guard every call with one mutex. When several chips share a bus, the port must also serialise the bus. See Contract . Editor setup ¶ The clang-format and clang-tidy configuration is in _config/ , and the repository root has no copy of it. Tools that take a path use it directly; CI does the same: Tool Setting Command line clang-format --style=file:_config/.clang-format , clang-tidy --config-file=_config/.clang-tidy -p build VS Code (C/C++ extension) "C_Cpp.clang_format_style": "file:${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-format" and "C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.args": ["--config-file=${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-tidy"] clangd (VS Code clangd, Neovim, Emacs), CLion These find .clang-format and .clang-tidy only by name, from the file upwards: copy both to the root once ( cp _config/.clang-format _config/.clang-tidy . ). .gitignore lists the copies, so they never reach a commit; copy again after _config/ changes Configure with -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON (clangd: --compile-commands-dir=build ) so the editor sees the same flags as the build.

Tools that take a path use it directly; CI does the same: Tool Setting Command line clang-format --style=file:_config/.clang-format , clang-tidy --config-file=_config/.clang-tidy -p build VS Code (C/C++ extension) "C_Cpp.clang_format_style": "file:${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-format" and "C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.args": ["--config-file=${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-tidy"] clangd (VS Code clangd, Neovim, Emacs), CLion These find .clang-format and .clang-tidy only by name, from the file upwards: copy both to the root once ( cp _config/.clang-format _config/.clang-tidy . ). .gitignore lists the copies, so they never reach a commit; copy again after _config/ changes Configure with -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON (clangd: --compile-commands-dir=build ) so the editor sees the same flags as the build.

The driver implements both completely behind one API: Config::protocol selects one for each Basis2 object, and the calls do not change. The driver uses one protocol per object and never mixes them. ASCII ¶ Every command starts with the unit ID, ends with a carriage return and gets one line in reply. The driver sends upper case only, and no command is started before the previous reply has ended and the line has been silent for 3.5 character times. The default Config addresses unit A . The parser splits on runs of spaces, accepts bracketed or bare flags, learns the layout (three or five numbers) from the first valid frame and rejects a later frame of the other layout. The manual shows only a controller's frame; the meter layout is an assumption. The replies to the setters, the error reply, the DV reply with several items, the gas list, VE and SN are not shown. The driver accepts the plausible forms and treats the ? token as Rejected . Three setters are checked: SetSetpoint() reads the value back (not while a ramp is active), SetGas() reads register 2100 back in Modbus mode and decodes the reply in ASCII mode (an undecodable reply is an error), and ChangeUnitId() reads the new ID back. Every other setter reports only that the instrument accepted it: no reply is Timeout , a ? is Rejected , and a lost reply to a write is never repeated. Each of these is an assumption recorded in the Datasheet map and settled by one capture from an instrument. Timing ¶ One character is ten bits. The reply wait is 3.5 character times, plus the line time of the longest reply of the command, plus processing_ms (50 ms), or slow_command_ms for commands that may write non-volatile memory. Baud 3.5 characters Poll reply wait 4800 7.3 ms 258 ms 9600 3.7 ms 154 ms 19200 1.8 ms 102 ms 38400 0.9 ms 76 ms 57600 0.6 ms 68 ms 115200 0.3 ms 60 ms These are derived from the character time, not measured. Modbus RTU ¶ Frames carry the address, a function code, data and a CRC-16 (polynomial 0xA001 , low byte first); registers are big-endian. The driver sends functions 3, 6 and 16 only, never to address 0 (broadcast) or above 247, never to a read-only register, and with the two magic values only on their registers: 0xAA55 to tare or reset the totalizer and 0x5214 to restore factory settings. A reply with a bad CRC, the wrong address or a function code with the high bit set (an exception) is an error, and the frame is discarded as a whole. Quantity Registers Scale Flow 2103 Signed 16 bit, decimals from Config::modbus_flow_decimals Total 2104 to 2105 Unsigned 32 bit, same decimals Temperature 2102 Signed, divided by 100 Valve drive 2107 Divided by 100 Status 2101 Bits as the flags above Setpoint 2053 to 2054 (write), 2106 (current) Signed 32 bit divided by 1000; the write completes when 2054 is written Gas 2100 Gas number Ramp 524 to 525 Percent of full scale per millisecond times 10^7 Watchdog 514 Milliseconds, 0 disables Setpoint source 516 0 analog, 1 digital saved, 2 digital unsaved Tare 39 (write 0xAA55 ), 51 (samples of about 2.5 ms) Firmware 25 256a + 16b + c The register table is inc/alicat_basis2_registers.hpp ; each row carries the firmware that added it, and a call that needs a newer firmware than the identity says returns FirmwareTooOld without sending ( Config::firmware_gate ). Differences you will see ¶ The flow, setpoint and total depend on the decimals you configured; a wrong value is off by a power of ten. The setpoint verify reads registers 2053 and 2054 back. Both they and 2106 report the ramped value while a ramp runs (M p.21), so the verify is skipped then ( VerifyPolicy::WhenNoRamp ). The ramp conversion from a rate and a time unit to percent per millisecond uses the manual's formula; the unit the ASCII command expects ("the default units of the loop control variable") is undefined in the manual, so the two protocols may differ for a ramp. Check a ramp on the bench. Reading register 4214 starts a measurement when trigger mode +4 is set; ReadPreviousMeasurement() warns in its documentation. Next: Safety notes .

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Run the driver on your PC first, with no hardware; then read the flow from your MCU: wire the instrument, write a small port class, call three driver functions. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Alicat Scientific, Inc. DOC-MANUAL-BASIS2 Rev 4: Models, ranges and options: Introduction, p. 3 Connector pins and serial levels: Power and Signal Connections (pin table), p. 7 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Try it on your PC ¶ examples/host/ runs the real driver against a simulated instrument, through a host port. From the repository root, with CMake and a C++20 compiler: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example cmake --build build-example ./build-example/alicat_basis2_host_example The program runs five short scenarios (read the flow, ramp a controller, tare and totalize, scan the line, read over Modbus) and exits with 0 when every call succeeded. The calls in main.cpp are the ones below; only the port differs on an MCU. CI builds and runs this example on every pull request. 1. Wire it ¶ MCU Instrument connector Notes UART TX pin 5 (RX or B) 38400 baud, 8N1; RS-232 or RS-485 levels by model, so a level shifter or a transceiver UART RX pin 6 (TX or A) 12 to 24 V supply pin 4 Power on pin 4 only. Any other pin can damage the instrument Ground pin 3 One common ground The Hardware page has the connector, both circuits and the warnings. Connect every pin before you switch on the supply. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the alicat_basis2::alicat_basis2 CMake target. Installation covers CMake on any MCU, the installed package and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-alicat-basis2.git external/driver-alicat-basis2 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code: it brings the UART up, moves bytes and tells the time. Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_port.hpp class MyPort : public alicat_basis2 :: UartInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the UART up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_uart_init (); } return ready_ ; } bool Write ( const uint8_t * data , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_uart_write ( data , len ); } // Whatever has arrived, up to `capacity` bytes. The driver polls, so do not wait for a full // frame. std :: size_t Read ( uint8_t * data , std :: size_t capacity , uint32_t timeout_ms ) noexcept { static_cast < void > ( timeout_ms ); return platform_uart_read ( data , capacity ); } // Drop stale bytes before each request. bool FlushInput () noexcept { return platform_uart_flush_input (); } // The driver times every wait against this clock. uint32_t NowMs () noexcept { return platform_millis (); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Porting explains each method, the optional hooks and the rules for RS-485. 4. Read the flow ¶ main.cpp #include "alicat_basis2.hpp" int read_flow ( MyPort & port , double & flow ) { alicat_basis2 :: Bus < MyPort > bus ( port ); alicat_basis2 :: Basis2 < MyPort > meter ( bus ); // unit ID 'A', 38400 baud, ASCII: the factory settings if ( auto r = meter . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // 1. the port comes up; no traffic yet return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); } if ( auto r = meter . Begin (); ! r ) { // 2. learn the instrument: Timeout means check wiring and unit ID return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); } const auto f = meter . ReadFlow (); // 3. one poll if ( ! f ) { return static_cast < int > ( f . error ); } flow = f . value . ToDouble (); // in the instrument's flow unit return 0 ; } What each step does: EnsureInitialized() calls your port's EnsureInitialized() . No traffic yet. Begin() learns the instrument: its kind (meter or controller), firmware, full scale, flow unit, gas and setpoint source. It sends read commands only. ReadFlow() sends one poll and returns the flow as a Decimal in the instrument's flow unit. The factory settings are unit ID A , 38400 baud, ASCII protocol. For another unit ID or for Modbus, change Config . This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check EnsureInitialized() returns Bus Your port's EnsureInitialized() : the UART did not come up Begin() returns Timeout Wiring, A and B swapped (RS-485), baud rate and unit ID ( Troubleshooting ) Begin() returns DeviceIdMismatch Another instrument answered: two instruments with one ID Begin() returns InvalidArgument In Modbus mode modbus_flow_decimals is required: set it ( Configuration ) Next ¶ API guide : setpoints, scanning, recovery, errors. Protocols : ASCII and Modbus RTU side by side. Configuration : every Config field and Kconfig. Examples : the host example and the ESP32 examples.

docs.text: Recurring defects ¶ The defects that reached an independent reviewer or the first CI run of more than one driver, one entry per class. Review skills cite these ids; the mechanization policy says where each class is caught and when it moves up a level. Append new findings to the entry they belong to, or add an entry (see the policy). Evidence names the driver, the review round ( reviews/<driver>-review<N>.md , finding id) or the CI run ( reports/<driver>-ci-*.txt ). Code examples are generic and minimal; none quotes a datasheet or a standard. Detection levels: lint (a script in the preflight or the gate, no judgement), test (a model knob, a mutation, a fuzz property or a compile-fail case that fails when the defect is present), review (a named reviewer asks one question). Status: enforced is in the template now; planned is the target, tracked in the policy's backlog, and until it lands the level below it (test, then review) is what protects the driver.
